question: Which statement best describes Page file?
options: A `layout` file wraps pages in its route segment. It is useful for shared navigation, sidebars, or consistent page framing. It is like a hallway connecting rooms on one floor. Layouts can preserve shared UI during navigation, so state placed there may live longer than page state. For example, a nested account layout can keep account tabs stable across child routes.

Nested layouts add shared structure for deeper route groups. A dashboard can have one outer site layout and a second layout for its own navigation. It is like a building with a common entrance and a separate office floor. Add nesting when it reflects real shared structure, not merely to create more files. For example, the root layout can load shared fonts and include the document language.

A `page` file defines the content shown at its route. The route comes from the folder path containing the file. It is like a room placed at a named address. Keep the page focused on what belongs at that destination, and verify direct visits and refreshes work. For example, a product page can own its product data while a shop layout owns shared navigation.

The root layout must include the document’s `<html>` and `<body>` elements. It is the outer shell for the application. It is like the building foundation that every room depends on. Set global metadata and shared providers at the right level, and avoid placing page-only content in the root. For example, do not put account-specific page text into a layout shared by unrelated routes.

Keep the page focused on what belongs at that destination, and verify direct visits and refreshes work. For example, a product page can own its product data while a shop layout owns shared navigation.
